title: Choose Taracine's new visual world
question: Redesign round. Your brief pins modern, aesthetic, easy to use. The roll assigned App Shell. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: App Shell
options.lineage: the native app language moviegoers already use daily: large-title headers, grouped lists, segmented controls, bottom tab bar, sheets
options.thesis: Taracine behaves like the cinema app on your phone, on the web: nothing to learn, one accent, posters carry all the color.
materials: poster art as the only imagery
options.viewport: Compact top bar with wordmark, cinema switcher pill and Sign in. A large title 'Now showing at Cubao' with today's date. A horizontal poster rail of today's films, each card showing its next three showtimes as tappable pills. Below: a segmented control (Now showing / Coming soon) over a clean poster grid. On phones a bottom tab bar (Home, Movies, Cinemas, Tickets, Account) and a sticky 'Buy tickets' bar on film pages.
options.risk: Familiar by design: it will look like a well-made app rather than a one-of-a-kind site. Poster art has to be strong or the page reads plain.

raised.raise: Preview before commit: the ticket summary builds live as you pick cinema, date and time, before Buy tickets is ever enabled.
Selecting a format highlights every showtime it governs and dims the rest.
Hard 4px grid and whole-pixel hairlines; no decorative blur or glow.
Past showtimes print struck-through inside their pill, never removed, so the day's shape stays legible.
Motion settles: only user actions animate; nothing moves at rest.

options.label: Super-app Flow
options.lineage: Grab, GCash and food-delivery booking flows Filipinos use every day
options.thesis: Booking a seat should feel like booking a ride: a stepper, big cards, one sticky action.
options.viewport: A three-step strip at the top (Movie → Cinema & time → Tickets), a search field, and a card list of films with poster, rating, and a green 'Pick a time' button; the chosen step's card expands in place.
options.risk: The most familiar modern landing for this audience, and the green-on-white reads like a ride-hailing app unless the posters dominate.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.lineage: a cloud edge diffracting sunlight into a narrow pastel fringe
options.thesis: An achromatic, airy page where color lives only in hairline edges and the active state.
options.viewport: Wide white margins, a quiet thin heading, film posters in a loose grid with a pastel fringe only on the selected card; showtimes as text rows with a violet band marking the next one.
options.case: Fuses cleanly into a modern minimalist language and holds the clarity axis. Loses on identification: a mall moviegoer reads it as a gallery, not a cinema, and thin type is weak on phones in bright light.
options.risk: Pretty but faint; the pastel fringe needs discipline or it becomes decoration.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.lineage: a printing darkroom under amber safelight
options.thesis: Booking as a chemical process in fixed stations.
options.viewport: Amber stations in order: compose, expose, develop, fix.
options.case: Amber-on-dark fails the brief's modern, easy-to-use pin and buries poster color.
options.kept: Preview before commit: a live ticket summary before Buy is enabled.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.lineage: early one-bit desktop with dithered grays
options.viewport: Overlapping film windows on a dither ground.
options.case: Retro and anti-modern; dithering destroys poster art.

options.label: Angura Poster
options.lineage: silkscreened underground theatre poster with ray burst
options.thesis: Showtimes packed into a ruled poster border.
options.viewport: A ray burst behind the lead film, dates packed in a border.
options.case: Loud and hand-made, the opposite of the brief's modern, easy pin.
options.kept: Past dates struck through inside their cell, never removed.

options.label: Character Sheet
options.lineage: amateur character reference sheet with swatch row
options.thesis: Films as reference sheets with swatches.
options.viewport: Four views and a swatch row per film.
options.case: Amateur aesthetic by definition; nothing here says cinema or ease.
options.kept: A selected format highlights every region it governs.

options.label: Plankton Wake
options.lineage: night sea lit by bioluminescent plankton
options.viewport: Pointer wakes glowing over a dark catalog.
options.case: Dark-with-neon-glow is the category rut and hard to read in a bright mall.
options.kept: Everything settles to rest; only user action animates.

canonCard.label: The cinema-chain standard
canonCard.thesis: What multiplex and streaming sites ship: dark UI, trailer-still hero, poster carousels, one red Buy Tickets button, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Trailer-still hero with a red CTA, a horizontal poster carousel, Now Showing / Coming Soon tabs, cinema dropdown.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every multiplex site by design.
